R366.summary: Ferdinand I writes to his envoy at the Porte, Johann Malvezzi, in reply to four of his letters; the clear text is the routine complaint about border raids, and the cipher carries the delicate matters. Rüstem Pasha has drawn great hatred on himself as author and defender of the Habsburg-Ottoman peace; the French are working to wreck that peace because, not daring to attack Charles V with their own forces, they want the Sultan's resources turned against him; and Malvezzi is to receive 1,500 ducats a year and 4,300 ducats at once through the secretary Justus de Argento.
R366.en:
p. 1. … the talks Rüstem Pasha held with you, namely that, on account of the treaty of peace begun with us, he has
drawn great hatred on himself, as the author of the making of that peace and now the promoter and defender of its
preservation; and moreover what you answered to whatever objections, questions and enquiries of the same Rüstem Pasha
…

p. 4. … that [they] will observe [it], the French trying so manifoldly and deceitfully to overturn this peace; who
indeed do this for no other reason than that, since the King of France and his like do not dare to provoke with their
own forces the sacred Imperial and Catholic royal Majesty, our dearest brother and lord, they may {avenge} themselves at
the expense of the Emperor of the {Turks} against His Imperial Majesty, who suffers nothing to be taken from him by
them beyond what is fair and honourable;

snip.cap: p. 4: graphic signs and null words running back into clear Latin
snip.credit: Hadtörténelmi Levéltár, Budapest, 1548/3, p. 4, via DECODE R366

system: Monoalphabetic homophonic cipher in graphic signs (alchemical and planetary signs, Greek and Latin letters with other values), two or three signs per common letter, numbers for doubled letters, and a short code list of syllables for the principals.
